correctness.rationale: For the saturated scalar CPT, Theorem 2 reduces \(O^*\) to the Euclidean distance from one cyclic shift to the affine hull of the others. Fourier diagonalization of the circulant orbit gives \((O^*)^2=n/\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}|\widehat x_k|^{-2}\) when all non-DC Fourier coefficients are nonzero, while any non-DC zero supplies an affine dependence and forces zero distance. For two ones at separation \(d\), \(|\widehat x_k|^2=4\cos^2(\pi kd/n)\). Writing \(N=n/\gcd(n,d)\), even \(N\) creates a zero; for odd \(N\), residue multiplicities and \(\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}\sec^2(\pi r/N)=N^2\) give the exact denominator \((nN-1)/4\). Independent least-squares calculations for \(n=20\) reproduced exactly the four positive separations and \(\sqrt{80/99}\), with error below \(3\times10^{-14}\).
